structure.note: One class of ordinary shares plus beneficiary certificates, which 'carry no economic rights and are issued to provide the holders of such certificates additional voting rights'; each carries one vote. Ten certificates were issued per ordinary share held of record by entities of the founders, 309,932,980 in total at December 31, 2025. The 20-F gives Daniel Ek 28.8% and Martin Lorentzon 40.5% of total voting power; no single holder is stated to have a majority.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (data.js fy 'Dec 2025'). Spotify reports under IFRS in euros, so values are billions of EUR (converted from € millions, no FX). Source is the FY2025 Form 20-F (accession 0001628280-26-006874); buybacks and stock comp match SEC XBRL. OWNERSHIP is as of December 31, 2025, from Item 7.A. LEADER: the 20-F lists Daniel Ek as 'Founder and Executive Chairman', with Alex Norström and Gustav Söderström as Co-Chief Executive Officers (Ek moved from CEO to Executive Chairman on January 1, 2026). PROXY SHARES: Ek's 28,625,267 ordinary shares (13.9%) are what the 20-F reports as his beneficial ownership. They include shares he only votes: footnote (1) says 11,993,298 are held by D.G.E. Investments, which he owns indirectly, and that he votes the shares held by TME Hong Kong, Image Frame, Tencent Mobility Limited and Distribution Pool Limited (all Tencent entities, 16,631,969 shares) through an irrevocable proxy held by D.G.E. Investments. 11,993,298 + 16,631,969 = 28,625,267, so the Tencent shares are inside his 13.9%. For reference only (computed, not stated in the filing): 11,993,298 / 205,832,527 is about 5.8%. TENCENT is listed in the 20-F at 16,631,969 ordinary shares, 8.1%. It is not added to largestHolders because those shares are already counted in Ek's figure (overlap rule). BENEFICIARY CERTIFICATES: Ek holds 119,932,980 (38.7%) and Lorentzon 190,000,000 (61.3%). They carry votes but no economic rights and are excluded from economic percentages. HOLDERS: Lorentzon's 9.3% includes 43,984 option shares exercisable within 60 days. Baillie Gifford, listed last year, no longer appears in the 5% table. DIVIDENDS: none ever paid. BUYBACKS: €439 million (US$510 million) for 768,223 shares under the repurchase program in 2025; the €241 million of employee taxes withheld on RSU releases is a separate line and excluded. STOCK COMP: the Note 5 personnel-expense line (€248 million, the XBRL-tagged figure); the cash-flow add-back is €247 million. PLAN: none described in the sections read.
